questions.question: What is the main purpose of visual hierarchy in a design?
choices: Guide viewers toward information in order of importance
Make every element equally prominent
Hide the main message
Match the file extension to the subject

questions.question: Which change most improves readability between text and its background?
choices: Use two similar pale colors
Increase contrast between the text and background
Add more decorative fonts
Shrink the text

questions.question: What does alignment help a designer achieve?
choices: A guaranteed color match
A larger image file
A clear visual relationship among elements
A consistent audio level

questions.question: Why might a designer repeat a color or shape across a layout?
choices: To remove all hierarchy
To make the design asymmetrical
To reduce the canvas size
To create consistency and connect related elements

questions.question: What is negative space?
choices: The area around and between visual elements
A region with a negative color value
A printing error
The darkest part of every image

questions.question: A poster has five unrelated fonts. What is a likely problem?
choices: The file becomes vector artwork
The typography may feel inconsistent and harder to scan
The colors become complementary
The message gains stronger hierarchy

questions.question: When is a grid especially useful?
choices: When choosing a camera lens
When editing spoken dialogue
When organizing content into consistent rows and columns
When compressing an audio file

questions.question: What does a logo need to do well at small sizes?
choices: Use many tiny details
Depend on a long caption
Include multiple photographs
Remain recognizable and legible

questions.question: Which pair is most likely to provide clear typographic contrast?
choices: A bold heading style paired with a readable body style
Two nearly identical display fonts
Several script fonts together
Body text in all capitals and italics

questions.question: Why should a designer consider the intended audience?
choices: Audience determines the computer's screen size
Audience needs influence language, imagery, and visual choices
Audience removes the need for a message
Audience always prefers the same colors

questions.question: What is a thumbnail sketch useful for?
choices: Exporting a finished vector logo
Checking copyright ownership
Testing layout ideas quickly before detailed production
Recording narration

questions.question: Which layout choice can make a call to action easier to find?
choices: Surround it with equally bold competing items
Hide it in dense body text
Use the same styling as the background
Give it clear placement and visual emphasis

questions.question: What does balance describe in a composition?
choices: How visual weight is distributed across the design
Whether a printer has enough paper
The number of colors in a palette
How fast an animation plays

questions.question: What is one benefit of limiting a design's color palette?
choices: It guarantees every color is accessible
It can strengthen unity and make choices feel intentional
It removes the need for contrast
It makes all images print identically

questions.question: Why should a designer test a layout on its actual display or print size?
choices: The test changes the topic
The layout cannot be resized later
Small details and text may behave differently at the final scale
It automatically adds a license

questions.question: What does proximity communicate in a layout?
choices: Every nearby element has equal importance
Text should always touch images
The design is intended for outdoors
Items placed near each other may be perceived as related

questions.question: A flyer has no clear focal point. What is a useful revision?
choices: Emphasize the most important message and reduce competing emphasis
Make every item larger
Add unrelated decoration
Remove all spacing

questions.question: What is a vector graphic's key advantage for many logos?
choices: It always contains photographic detail
It can scale without becoming pixelated
It cannot be edited
It stores sound more efficiently

questions.question: How can a designer check color accessibility?
choices: Choose colors only by personal preference
Make all text the same hue
Use a contrast checker and avoid relying on color alone
Convert every element to a photograph

questions.question: What should a design brief clarify before production begins?
choices: The final number of social media likes
A complete list of all possible fonts
The printer's location only
The goal, audience, message, and practical constraints
